characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: The Technical Feasibility Strategy lever aims to demonstrate the technical feasibility of platform-neutral and fallback-capable Danish digital identity systems. This involves building demonstrators that showcase secure authentication methods, such as FIDO2 on mainstream Android devices or browser-based fallbacks. The goal is to provide concrete evidence that supports policy traction and enhances credibility in procurement negotiations.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever has strong synergy with the Policy Advocacy Strategy (80b177d0-c67e-4bc2-bd50-3f49b815e633) as it provides the technical foundation for advocating for platform-neutral standards. It also aligns with the Procurement Influence Strategy (f1c0d856-0cfc-4def-ab68-c58bb8b17551) by providing a feasible and secure alternative to traditional digital identity systems.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever may conflict with the Coalition Building Strategy (1731ad9a-c471-40de-9b90-12f23721aebd) as it requires a focused approach, potentially limiting the breadth of support. Additionally, it may create trade-offs with the Procurement Influence Strategy as the cost implications of each demonstrator approach are not explicitly addressed.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: The Policy Advocacy Strategy lever aims to shape procurement policies and influence AltID requirements by reframing the issue in terms of continuity of service, supplier concentration risks, and democratic accountability. This involves balancing continuity arguments with privacy concerns and broadening the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever has strong synergy with the Technical Feasibility Strategy (bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474) as it relies on concrete evidence from demonstrators to support policy traction. It also aligns with the Procurement Influence Strategy (f1c0d856-0cfc-4def-ab68-c58bb8b17551) by influencing procurement policies and requirements.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever may conflict with the Coalition Building Strategy (1731ad9a-c471-40de-9b90-12f23721aebd) as it requires a broad coalition, potentially diluting focus. Additionally, it may create trade-offs with the EU Standards Engagement Strategy (2e9016aa-8563-447e-a5e0-0e146f4ebad3) as regulatory capture by incumbent vendors is not considered.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: The Coalition Building Strategy lever aims to build a strong coalition of stakeholders, including security experts, contingency-planning stakeholders, civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers. This involves actively recruiting dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever has strong synergy with the Policy Advocacy Strategy (80b177d0-c67e-4bc2-bd50-3f49b815e633) as it provides a broad coalition that supports policy traction. It also aligns with the Procurement Influence Strategy (f1c0d856-0cfc-4def-ab68-c58bb8b17551) by influencing procurement policies and requirements.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever may conflict with the Technical Feasibility Strategy (bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474) as it requires a focused approach, potentially limiting the breadth of support. Additionally, it may create trade-offs with the EU Standards Engagement Strategy (2e9016aa-8563-447e-a5e0-0e146f4ebad3) as conflicting priorities within the coalition are not addressed.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: The Procurement Influence Strategy lever aims to influence AltID procurement policies and requirements by including platform-neutral language or specific requirements for certified fallback authentication paths. This involves advocating for a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever has strong synergy with the Technical Feasibility Strategy (bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474) as it relies on concrete evidence from demonstrators to support procurement influence. It also aligns with the Policy Advocacy Strategy (80b177d0-c67e-4bc2-bd50-3f49b815e633) by influencing procurement policies and requirements.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever may conflict with the Coalition Building Strategy (1731ad9a-c471-40de-9b90-12f23721aebd) as it requires a focused approach, potentially limiting the breadth of support. Additionally, it may create trade-offs with the EU Standards Engagement Strategy (2e9016aa-8563-447e-a5e0-0e146f4ebad3) as vendors may game the procurement process.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: The EU Standards Engagement Strategy lever aims to engage with relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards. This involves championing a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever has strong synergy with the Policy Advocacy Strategy (80b177d0-c67e-4bc2-bd50-3f49b815e633) as it relies on policy traction to support EU standards engagement. It also aligns with the Procurement Influence Strategy (f1c0d856-0cfc-4def-ab68-c58bb8b17551) by influencing procurement policies and requirements.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever may conflict with the Coalition Building Strategy (1731ad9a-c471-40de-9b90-12f23721aebd) as it requires a focused approach, potentially limiting the breadth of support. Additionally, it may create trade-offs with the Technical Feasibility Strategy (bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474) as EU standards are not immune to influence by large platform vendors.
